issues.t: Dual-clutch transmission shudder and jerky low-speed driving
issues.sym: Shudder or a lurch when pulling away, slow or clunky engagement into Drive or Reverse, a jolt between 2nd and 3rd gear on light throttle, or slipping. It can get worse until the car won't drive.
issues.why: The GLA uses an automated dual-clutch gearbox. Its wet clutch packs wear, its fluid degrades, and its mechatronic control unit can fail. Stop-and-go driving and skipped fluid services speed this up; trouble often starts around 40,000 to 75,000 miles.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the latest transmission software. A fluid and filter change with a clutch adaptation reset often clears early shudder. If it slips, get a transmission specialist's diagnosis before it leaves you stranded.

issues.t: Electric water pump failure and overheating
issues.sym: The temperature gauge spikes and a coolant warning lights up, often suddenly with no earlier sign. The heater may also blow cool air.
issues.why: The water pump's motor or plastic impeller breaks, so coolant stops flowing. The electronic thermostat also wears out.
issues.next: Pull over and turn the engine off as soon as it overheats; driving on can ruin the head gasket. Replace the pump and thermostat together.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine for a few seconds after a cold start, sometimes with a check engine light and camshaft sensor codes.
issues.why: The hydraulic chain tensioner can bleed down overnight, so the chain slaps until oil pressure builds. Long oil change intervals and low oil stretch the chain.
issues.next: Have it checked before the chain stretches enough to jump a tooth. Keep oil changes on time with Mercedes-approved oil.

issues.t: Turbocharger wear or failure
issues.sym: Blue or gray smoke under acceleration, whining or grinding from the turbo, and power loss.
issues.why: Turbo bearings wear out early when oil changes are stretched, the wrong oil is used, or the engine is driven hard while still cold.
issues.next: Have the turbo and oil supply checked. Fixing it early stops debris and oil from damaging the engine and exhaust.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, misfires and less power, mostly at low engine speeds.
issues.why: With direct fuel injection, fuel doesn't wash the intake valves, so oil vapor from the crankcase vent bakes onto them.
issues.next: If misfire codes point to carbon, have the intake valves cleaned (walnut blasting). Regular highway drives and on-time oil changes help.

issues.t: Camshaft welds can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, noise from the top of the engine, a stall, or an engine that won't restart.
issues.why: Camshafts in some GLA 250s built July 17 to August 31, 2015 were welded out of specification and could break. Mercedes recalled them for free camshaft replacement.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall at a dealer or nhtsa.gov.

issues.t: Driver airbag could deploy unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: Often an airbag warning light from a broken clockspring. Rarely, the driver airbag could go off without a crash.
issues.why: Steering column parts were not grounded well enough. With a broken clockspring, static electricity could set off the driver airbag. Mercedes added grounding under recall.
issues.next: Check that the recall was done. If the airbag light is on, have it diagnosed; the recall does not replace a broken clockspring.

issues.t: Steering shaft joint bearing can separate (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or free play in the steering, or knocking felt through the steering wheel.
issues.why: The bearing bore in the steering shaft's universal joint allows too much movement, so the bearing and joint can separate over time, risking loss of steering control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall right away and have the free repair done. Get any new steering clunk checked before driving far.

issues.t: Front roof panel can come loose after a repair (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or a lifting edge at the front of the panoramic roof. In the worst case the panel could detach while driving.
issues.why: On cars with a panoramic roof, the front roof panel may not have been bonded correctly during an earlier repair. Mercedes recalled affected cars to replace it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall, especially if the roof or windshield was ever repaired.

issues.t: Rearview camera image doesn't show (recall)
issues.sym: No camera picture appears when reversing, or the infotainment screen goes black and restarts.
issues.why: Software errors in the camera system and, on 2021 models, the MBUX infotainment system could stop the camera image from showing. Mercedes fixed both with free software updates.
issues.next: Make sure the software updates were installed by a dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Emergency call (eCall) may not work (recall)
issues.sym: An SOS system warning may appear, or there may be no sign. After a crash the car might not call for help or might send the wrong location.
issues.why: Software errors in the communication module and its SIM card could disable the emergency call system or send the wrong location.
issues.next: Make sure the free software updates were done, over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: Driver door lock switch can corrode, risking rollaway (recall)
issues.sym: No warning that the driver's door is open, and the parking brake or Auto-Park doesn't set itself when the door opens.
issues.why: A small switch inside the driver's door lock can corrode and fail to sense an open door, so the automatic parking brake may not engage. Mercedes is replacing the lock for free.
issues.next: Always shift to Park and set the parking brake yourself until the recall is done. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or knocking from a rear wheel, or weaker braking.
issues.why: Fasteners on the rear brake caliper housing may not have been tightened properly, so brake parts could loosen or come off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the free inspection done.

issues.t: Coolant line leak and coolant warning
issues.sym: A coolant level warning, coolant smell, or coolant dripping under the front of the car.
issues.why: A coolant line can leak, partly from high pressure in the cooling system. Mercedes has a bulletin and a service campaign covering early cars of this generation.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and ask the dealer whether the campaign covers your VIN. Don't drive if it overheats.

issues.t: Fuel smell from leaking fuel supply hose
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell around the car or inside the cabin.
issues.why: Mercedes extended the warranty on the fuel supply hose for these SUVs, and fuel smell in the cabin is one of the most reported GLA 250 complaints.
issues.next: Fuel smells are a fire risk, so have it checked promptly and ask the dealer whether the extended hose coverage applies.

issues.t: Dead battery or car won't unlock after sitting
issues.sym: The car won't unlock or start, shows a 'Battery - Start Engine' message, or the battery is dead after a few days parked.
issues.why: A Mercedes bulletin traces this to a module that keeps the car's data network awake after parking, draining the battery.
issues.next: Charge or jump the battery, then have a dealer check for software updates and test the battery.

issues.t: Creaking or grinding from steering column
issues.sym: Creaking, squeaking or grinding when turning the wheel, or a grinding between the wheel and the stalks.
issues.why: Mercedes has several bulletins on steering column noises, including a squeaking input shaft caused by too little grease.
issues.next: Have the dealer check it against the bulletins; the fix is usually lubrication or a part under warranty.

issues.t: Front brakes squeak
issues.sym: Squeaking from the front brakes when braking, whether the brakes are hot or cold.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin blaming friction between the brake pad lining and the caliper.
issues.next: Mention the bulletin to the dealer. Have the pads checked if the noise turns into grinding.

issues.t: Humming or vibration from rear axle when maneuvering
issues.sym: A hum or vibration from the rear when parking, turning tightly or pulling away on 4MATIC all-wheel-drive models.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin for rear axle noise when maneuvering, plus another for communication faults with the all-wheel-drive control unit.
issues.next: Have a dealer check it against the bulletins while the car is under warranty.

issues.t: Side windows squeak or crack when moving
issues.sym: Door windows move stiffly and make cracking or squeaking noises.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin tracing this to the sealing lip of the inner window seal.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to fix it under the bulletin while under warranty.

issues.t: Headlights aimed incorrectly (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights that seem to light the road poorly or dazzle oncoming drivers.
issues.why: A small number of 2022 GLA 250 and AMG GLA 35 models left the factory with headlights incorrectly adjusted.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the free headlight aim done.
